solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Back bedroom's outside falls away eroded, affected by bad weather

indicators.note: back here asks for what follows, bedroom's edges plus the falls-away word, to be read from right to left
the outside of a word is its two end letters, so only the edges of bedroom are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of bedroom
something that rots decays and falls away
eroded rock has been eaten away

explanation.surface: A dilapidated house where the back bedroom's outer wall is crumbling away in the weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' governs only the first two pieces; the eroded word follows unturned.
explanation.definitionFit: Something storm-beaten has been battered and damaged by rough conditions such as gales and rain.

clue.text: Sniper woman admitting to murder alongside car

parts.note: bus is informal for a car or other vehicle

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the woman word takes the murder word inside it

parts.note: her is the pronoun for a woman
to whack someone is slang for killing them

explanation.surface: A female sniper who confesses to a killing committed beside a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alongside' sets the car word beside the woman-and-murder combination, at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A bushwhacker is a guerrilla who ambushes enemies from cover, firing on them unseen, which is what a sniper does.

clue.text: Practice before work at hives

parts.note: ure is an old word for use or practice
to do a task is to work at it

explanation.surface: Training before getting down to work among the beehives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' simply places the practice word first. 'hives' looks like bees' homes but is the skin rash.
explanation.definitionFit: Uredo is an old medical name for urticaria, the itchy rash of raised weals commonly called hives.

clue.text: Try and sue crooked sponsor

indicators.note: something crooked is bent out of shape, so the letters are twisted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice to take a dishonest backer to court.
explanation.definitionFit: A surety is a person who takes on responsibility for another's debt or conduct, acting as guarantor or sponsor.

clue.text: Gallagher brother retracted after he bites at undesirable post

indicators.note: something that bites takes a mouthful, so he closes around at

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: retracted means drawn back, so the brother's name is read backwards

parts.note: Liam Gallagher, singer of the band Oasis, whose brother is Noel

explanation.surface: Oasis's feuding Gallagher brothers, one lashing out at the other over some unwelcome post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts the reversed brother second, behind the he-and-at combination.
explanation.definitionFit: Hate mail is abusive or threatening letters, exactly the kind of correspondence nobody wants to receive.

clue.text: Crash killing cat in Welsh city

indicators.note: killing gets rid of the cat, so its letters are taken out of the city

parts.note: Wrexham is a city in north Wales
the Rex is a breed of curly-coated cat

explanation.surface: A road crash in a Welsh city that killed a cat.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing REX from the middle of WREXHAM leaves the two ends, W and HAM, which close up.
explanation.definitionFit: Wham is the sound of a heavy blow or collision, so it serves as a word for a crash.

clue.text: Golf club sockets bound to lose power, plugs not active

indicators.note: to lose power means the letter for power is dropped from the bound word

parts.note: a hop is a bound or leap
P is the symbol for power in physics

indicators.note: not active means the abbreviation for active is taken out of the plugs word

parts.note: a plug seals a hole, so plugs means seals
A is a standard abbreviation for active

explanation.surface: Golf club heads whose sockets are sure to lose their drive.
explanation.walkthrough: HOP loses P to leave HO; SEALS loses A to leave SELS; together HOSELS.
explanation.definitionFit: A hosel is the hollow neck on an iron's head into which the shaft fits, so hosels are golf club sockets.

clue.text: Box carrying jade pony in NA?

indicators.note: a box carrying something holds it inside, so jade goes within

parts.note: a case is a box
yu is a Chinese word for jade found in Chambers

explanation.surface: A box with a jade pony figurine inside, perhaps bought in North America.
explanation.walkthrough: NA is North America; the question mark flags that the definition is an example of where the pony lives.
explanation.definitionFit: A cayuse is a small native horse of western North America, named after the Cayuse people of Oregon.

clue.text: Member of ground crew announcing critical leak

indicators.note: announcing is speaking out, so what counts is how the words sound, not how they are spelt

parts.note: something critical is key
to take a leak is slang for passing urine, a wee

explanation.surface: An airfield worker announcing a dangerous fuel leak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground crew' suggests airport staff; in RAF slang a kiwi is a non-flying officer, named after the flightless bird.
explanation.definitionFit: In Royal Air Force slang, a kiwi is a member of the ground staff, because like the bird they never fly.

clue.text: Starts to experience visitation then séance drifts to fade away

indicators.note: starts are opening letters, so only the first letter of each following word is kept

parts.note: the first letters of experience and visitation

indicators.note: drifts suggests letters wandering about, so the word séance is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the accent

explanation.surface: A ghostly visitation at a séance gradually drifting away, like a spirit fading.
explanation.definitionFit: To evanesce is to vanish gradually, like vapour, from the Latin for disappearing.

clue.text: Leaving street drive from end to end

indicators.note: leaving here means going away from, so the street abbreviation departs the drive word

parts.note: thrust is driving force
St is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: Leaving a road and driving all the way along another.
explanation.definitionFit: Thru is the informal, mainly American spelling of through, meaning all the way across or along.

clue.text: Give up and marry before accepting answer

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the marry word holds the answer abbreviation

parts.note: to wive is an old verb meaning to marry
A is the abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: Giving up a single life and marrying before getting a yes.
explanation.definitionFit: To waive a right or claim is to relinquish it voluntarily, giving it away.

clue.text: The night before take care about changing past camping gear

parts.note: the eve is the night before a festival or event

indicators.note: about means around, so the care word wraps around the rearranged past

parts.note: reck is an old verb meaning to heed or take care

indicators.note: changing alters the order of the letters of past

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Packing carefully the night before a camping trip.
explanation.definitionFit: An Everest pack is a rucksack on a light frame, a piece of kit carried by hikers and campers.

clue.text: Public appeal to demand too much work?

parts.note: overt means open, public
an ask is a request or appeal

explanation.surface: A public plea against bosses who demand excessive work.
explanation.definitionFit: To overtask someone is to give them more duties than they can manage, overloading them with labour.

clue.text: About to return reward to cash in

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the reward word is read backwards

parts.note: meed is an old word for a reward

explanation.surface: Someone about to bring back a voucher to exchange it for money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' reads as 'on the point of', but About is the word giving RE and 'to' joins the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To redeem a token or bond is to exchange it for its cash value.

clue.text: Lease's ending on Scottish girl's pad perhaps

indicators.note: an ending is the final letter, so only the last letter of lease's is used

parts.note: the last letter of lease
quine is a Scots word for a girl or young woman

explanation.surface: A lease ending on a young Scottish woman's flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pad' looks like a flat; it is an old word for an easy-paced horse. 'on' places the E before the girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A pad is a road horse, and an equine is any member of the horse family, so a pad is one example.

clue.text: Aspirant, pale imitation ultimately a drone?

parts.note: wan means pale

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of imitation is used

parts.note: the last letter of imitation
taken as written
a drone is a male bee

explanation.surface: A would-be star who is only a pale imitation, in the end just a drone.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a drone is one kind of bee.
explanation.definitionFit: A wannabe, also spelt wannabee, is someone who aspires to be like a celebrity or group, an aspirant.

clue.text: Boisterous result after Blimp's let loose?

definitions.text: Boisterous result after Blimp's let loose?

indicators.note: to let something go is to release it, so loose is dropped from the cartoon colonel's name

parts.note: Colonel Blimp, the pompous cartoon reactionary
limp means slack, floppy, loose

indicators.note: something boisterous is rowdy and disorderly, so the letters of result are thrown about

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The noisy outcome when Colonel Blimp lets rip.
explanation.walkthrough: Colonel Blimp is a British cartoon icon of the pompous blustering reactionary, which is why the whole clue also defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bluster is loud, aggressive, empty talk, the kind of noisy bombast a Blimp-like figure produces when he gets going.

clue.text: Last of many idiots uncovered hollow truth

indicators.note: uncovered means stripped of its covering, so the outer letters of the idiots word go

parts.note: numpty is British, originally Scottish, slang for a fool

indicators.note: hollow means emptied of its inside, so only the outer letters of truth remain

parts.note: the first and last letters of truth

explanation.surface: A sceptic's verdict: the last of a crowd of fools, exposed, has only empty truths.
explanation.walkthrough: NUMPTIES loses its first and last letters to give UMPTIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Umptieth means the latest of a great many in a series, as in telling someone for the umptieth time.

clue.text: Hindu traders taking sauna baths round Norway

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the baths word goes around the Norway abbreviation

parts.note: a banya is a Russian steam bath or sauna
N is the international vehicle code for Norway

explanation.surface: Indian merchants relaxing in Scandinavian-style steam baths.
explanation.definitionFit: Banyans, or banians, are Hindu merchants or traders, especially of a caste that abstains from meat.

clue.text: Escape room experience ultimately to enjoy

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the final letters of room and experience are kept

parts.note: the last letters of room and experience
to enjoy a right is to have the use of it

explanation.surface: Someone's verdict on an escape room: what matters in the end is having fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Escape room' reads as one phrase, but Escape alone is the definition and room gives only its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A meuse is a gap in a hedge through which a hunted animal slips away, hence a means of getting away.

clue.text: Mushroom ramen OK in part

indicators.note: in part means only a portion of the words is used, so the answer lies inside them

parts.note: the run of letters across ramen and OK
the first letter of in

explanation.surface: A judgement that a bowl of Japanese noodles is passable, partly.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs through ram(EN OK I)n.
explanation.definitionFit: Enoki are thin white Japanese mushrooms with long stems, often added to ramen and other noodle soups.

clue.text: Stink about place repulsed Falkland islander

indicators.note: repulsed means driven back, so the whole combination is read backwards
about means around, so the stink word goes around the place abbreviation

parts.note: a reek is a strong bad smell
Pl is the abbreviation for place in addresses

explanation.surface: A smell around a place that drives people back.
explanation.walkthrough: RE(PL)EK, read upwards in this down entry, gives KELPER.
explanation.definitionFit: Kelper is the nickname for a native of the Falkland Islands, from the kelp seaweed that surrounds the islands.

clue.text: Digestive organs a little poorly turning septic

indicators.note: a little of a word is just a bit of it, here its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of poorly

indicators.note: turning means changing, so the letters of septic are reshuffled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A patient's stomach is a bit poorly and an infection is setting in.
explanation.definitionFit: Peptics, in Chambers, are the digestive organs, from peptic meaning relating to digestion.

clue.text: I ease off reversing boat on Ganges

indicators.note: reversing turns the order round, so the words are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
to let up is to ease off

explanation.surface: A boatman slowing down by backing his boat on the Ganges.
explanation.definitionFit: A puteli is a flat-bottomed cargo boat used on the Ganges in India.

clue.text: Remote access system clear after return of cancelled service

indicators.note: return means coming back, so the cancelled-service word is read backwards

parts.note: in tennis a let is a serve that clips the net and is replayed, so it does not count
net profit is what is cleared after costs

explanation.surface: A computer link working again after a cancelled service is restored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' suggests a train or utility, but the cancelled service is a tennis serve that must be replayed.
explanation.definitionFit: Telnet is a network protocol letting a user log in to and operate a distant computer through a text terminal.

clue.text: Exercise repeated t.i.d., putting jelly in bum

indicators.note: putting one thing in another places it inside, so jelly goes within the bum word

parts.note: the anus is the bottom's opening
a gel is a jelly

explanation.surface: A prescription: an exercise three times a day, plus a gel applied rectally.
explanation.walkthrough: t.i.d. is the medical prescription abbreviation for three times a day, which fits the surface's doctor's note.
explanation.definitionFit: The Angelus is a Catholic devotion recited at morning, noon and evening, so it is a spiritual exercise said thrice daily.

clue.text: Sister left in charge

indicators.note: in places the left abbreviation inside the charge word

parts.note: something in your charge is in your care
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A nun who has been left running things.
explanation.definitionFit: A Clare is a nun of the order of Poor Clares founded by Saint Clare of Assisi, a religious sister.

clue.text: Time to divide loft in SW corner

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
to allot is to share out or divide

explanation.surface: Time to split up the attic space in the south-west corner of the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'SW corner' sounds like part of a room; it means the south-west of England, where the word is dialect.
explanation.definitionFit: A tallot is a hayloft in the dialect of south-west England, so it is a regional word for a loft.

clue.text: Pot close to a fortune

parts.note: your lot is your fortune or destiny
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cooking pot worth nearly a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to' places the two pieces side by side, with A after LOT in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A lota is a small round brass or copper water vessel used in India, a kind of pot.

clue.text: Encouragement to satisfy mostly with kiss

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the satisfy word loses its last letter

parts.note: to fill a need is to satisfy it
to lip is an old verb meaning to kiss

explanation.surface: A kiss as the encouragement that nearly satisfies.
explanation.definitionFit: A fillip is a stimulus or boost that perks someone up, which is a form of encouragement.

clue.text: Father to run over Scottish paddock

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title

indicators.note: over in a down clue means turned upwards, so the run word is read backwards

parts.note: to go is to run, as an engine does

explanation.surface: A priest hurrying across a field in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'paddock' looks like a field; in Scots a paddock or puddock is a frog or toad.
explanation.definitionFit: Paddock is an old and Scottish word for a frog or toad, so the answer is what the Scots word names.

clue.text: Pastoral work dated around start of Renaissance given to Academy

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the dated word encloses that letter

parts.note: a couple who are seeing each other are dating, so seen means dated

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, so only the opening letter of Renaissance is used

parts.note: the first letter of Renaissance
to and at both mark where someone is going or is, as in 'off to the Academy'
A is an abbreviation for Academy

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned pastoral painting from the early Renaissance donated to the Royal Academy.
explanation.walkthrough: SE(R)EN is followed by AT and A; 'Pastoral work' suggests a painting but the work is musical.
explanation.definitionFit: A serenata is an eighteenth-century cantata, often on a pastoral theme, performed as an evening musical entertainment.

clue.text: Tense scene about coming out hit high notes

indicators.note: something hit is knocked about, so the letters are rearranged
coming out means leaving, so the about abbreviation leaves the scene word

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
taken as written
c, for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A tense scene in an opera as the singer comes out and hits the high notes.
explanation.walkthrough: SCENE without C leaves SENE; with T, those letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greek music the nete was the highest string or note of the lyre, so netes are high notes.

clue.text: Roll of highly glazed fabric's fine

indicators.note: a roll turns something over, so the fabric word is read backwards

parts.note: ciré is a fabric with a high-gloss waxed finish

explanation.surface: A bolt of shiny fabric described as fine cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fine' looks like an adjective praising the fabric; it is a noun, a penalty payment.
explanation.definitionFit: An eric was the blood money paid in old Irish law by a killer to the victim's family, a fine for the offence.

clue.text: Read the sign wrongly like Mr Magoo?

indicators.note: wrongly signals an error in order, so the letters of the phrase are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Mr Magoo misreading a sign, as he always does.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Magoo is an American cartoon character, a short-sighted old man who blunders into scrapes because he cannot see.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearsighted means able to see only close things clearly, the defining trait of the cartoon character.
